cohort: 5,081 cases of childhood ALL and 18,927 matched controls born in California between 1978 and 2009
finding: Elective cesarean section was associated with a significantly elevated risk of childhood ALL (odds ratio (OR) = 1.17, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.01, 1.36).
mod_finding: Elective cesarean section was associated with a significantly elevated risk of childhood ALL, particularly at peak ages of incidence (2-4 years), while emergency C-section was not associated with childhood ALL.
